description.value: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled longitudinal study used continuous arterial spin-labeled perfusion fMRI to examine the effects of a 3-week varenicline regimen on cerebral blood flow during smoking-cue exposure and at rest in nonabstinent smokers.

spans.text: To quantify the effects of long-term administration of varenicline on the resting brain and on the brain’s responses during exposure to smoking cues, we implemented a laboratory model of conditioned responding and the technique of continuous arterial spin-labeled (CASL) perfusion functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to image nonabstinent smokers before and after a 3-week double-blind randomized placebo-controlled medication regimen.

value: we hypothesized that varenicline would have a third mechanism to blunt responses to smoking cues in the reward-related ventral striatum and medial orbitofrontal cortex and would be associated with a reduction in smoking cue–elicited craving
We predicted that varenicline-induced activation of the LOFC in the brain at rest would correlate with diminished neural responses during exposure to smoking cues.

spans.text: We hypothesize that varenicline would have a third mechanism to blunt responses to smoking cues in the reward-related ventral striatum and medial orbitofrontal cortex and would be associated with a reduction in smoking cue–elicited craving.

description.value: Smokers were randomized in a double-blind study to receive varenicline or placebo and were scanned before randomization and on day 21 of medication administration.
